name: aseman-peyda
description: Brings up Aseman Peyda on Decillion: the aseman-peyda organization with its team, platform and operations key; a project with the Peyda Analyst and Peyda Builder agents; Peyda itself (GLiNER2 query extraction, the iran-mcp gateway, the agentic loop and its Elpian frontend) installed, tested and published as the platform's frontend. Every entity is an upsert: run it again and it creates what is missing, updates what changed and leaves the rest.

org.description: The developer organization (team) that owns the platform

product.description: The platform's product: the search engine

team.description: Handles to invite to the organization as developers

agent_model.description: The agents' model, exactly as the node's LLM provider lists it (Admin panel > LLM providers). Empty keeps each agent's current model, and a new agent gets the node's fallback, gpt-4o-mini, which many providers do not offer: set this if the run fails with 'model ... is not offered by ...'

gliner_model.description: The GLiNER2 checkpoint that reads queries. The multilingual one reads Persian; fastino/gliner2.5-base-v1 is English-only

max_rounds.description: How many extract → search → review rounds the agentic loop may take for one message

default_city.description: The city assumed for location-bound services (food, groceries) when a query names none

node_url.description: The node's public address as the project's computer reaches it, for example https://preview.decillionai.com. Set it when the chat shows 'The analyst was unavailable' with 'Name or service not known': the node hands apps an internal host name (http://decillion:8080) that a computer outside its network cannot resolve. Empty uses the address the node gives. Changing it alone does not rebuild the frontend: also pass rebuild_frontend=true

build_frontend.description: Have the Builder agent turn the prepared project into the platform's frontend and publish it

rebuild_frontend.description: Rebuild the frontend even when its source is unchanged

manage_network.description: Open the project's network to what Peyda needs (package and model downloads, the iran-mcp sites) when the node restricts it; adds hosts to the project's allowlist, never removes any. false: leave the project's policy alone

egress_allow.description: Extra hosts to allow (for example an API host a site uses that is not on its main domain); patterns like *.example.com work

hf_endpoint.description: A Hugging Face mirror's URL (for example https://hf-mirror.com) for the GLiNER2 model download, when huggingface.co cannot be reached from the node's network. Empty: huggingface.co

google_maps.description: Add Google Maps as a search service (places and local businesses: address, phone, website, rating), in plain and agentic search, through the Google Maps Scraper Kit's engine (a pinned copy and a headless Chrome are installed on the project's computer). false: skip it

IRAN_PROXY_URL.description: An HTTP proxy with an Iranian address. Many iran-mcp sites answer only Iranian connections; without it those services report errors and the rest still work

HF_TOKEN.description: A Hugging Face token, only to speed up the model download

GMAPS_PROXY_URL.description: A proxy for the Google Maps engine's Chrome (http://user:pass@host:port, or socks5://host:port without a password), when Google refuses or rate-limits the computer's address. Not the Iranian proxy: Google Maps does not need one

agent_in_space.description: An agent, upserted by name, and installed in a space (also upserted)

steps.name: Operations API key (platform write, models, usage)

with.name: ${{ inputs.product }}
with.description: Where ${{ inputs.product }}, the search engine of ${{ inputs.platform_name }}, is built and run

steps.name: Where may the project's computer connect?
Does the network policy need more hosts?

set.egress_fix: ${{ inputs.manage_network && steps.egress_now.outputs.policy.mode != 'allow_all' && (steps.egress_now.outputs.policy.mode == 'deny_all' || any(vars.egress_hosts, h => !contains(steps.egress_now.outputs.policy.allow ?? list(), h))) }}

steps.name: Allow what Peyda needs (adds to the allowlist, removes nothing)
The computer's proxy reads its policy every 30 s
Put Peyda's source on the project's computer and start the install in the background
Wait for the install: environment, model, iran-mcp servers, Google Maps engine, tests, smoke test

assert.message:
The install did not finish. Its log, from the project's computer:
${{ steps.install_wait.outputs.output }}

steps.name: Which source is the published app built from?
The Builder adopts the prepared project as the platform's app (skipped when it is current)
Apps the agents have built, now

assert.message: no app titled Peyda was built in the project: read the Peyda Builder's reply (steps.frontend_build) and the run log, fix, and run the installer again

steps.name: Publish it as the platform's frontend (only when it is not already)

assert.message: the organization and its platform exist
the Peyda Analyst and the Peyda Builder are in the project
the frontend is published on the platform

on_failure.log: Stopped at ${{ failure.path }}: ${{ failure.message }}. Nothing was rolled back: every step is an upsert, so fix the cause and run the installer again (or resume from run ${{ run.id }}).
